defaults.permitted_development: A loft conversion can fall within Class B permitted development in England if the roof enlargement stays within the roof-space allowance, does not project beyond the principal roof slope facing a highway and keeps to the Class B conditions. On deeper rural plots, the harder issues are often prominence in open views, out-of-scale massing and how the addition reads from lanes or public footpaths.

rules.height_rules: No part of the enlargement should rise above the highest part of the existing roof. Raising the ridge usually moves the scheme out of permitted development.
rules.depth_rules: Keep dormers and other roof projections within the roof-space allowance: up to 40 cubic metres on a terraced house or 50 cubic metres otherwise, taking earlier roof enlargements into account.
rules.boundary_rules: Side-facing windows should be obscure glazed and non-opening below 1.7m, and overlooking can still become a problem where rooflights or dormers directly face nearby homes. On deeper rural plots, the harder issues are often prominence in open views, out-of-scale massing and how the addition reads from lanes or public footpaths.
rules.roof_rules: The enlargement must not project beyond the existing roof slope on the principal elevation facing a highway. Other than hip-to-gable work, it should be set back at least 20cm from the eaves and should not create a balcony or roof terrace.
rules.materials_rules: External materials should be similar in appearance to the existing house so the work reads as part of the original roof rather than a top-heavy bolt-on. rules.depth_rules: Keep dormers and other roof projections within the roof-space allowance: up to 40 cubic metres on a terraced house or 50 cubic metres on a detached or semi-detached house, taking earlier roof enlargements into account.
rules.boundary_rules: Side-facing windows should be obscure glazed and non-opening below 1.7m, and rooflights or dormers that look directly into neighbouring rooms or gardens can still create overlooking issues.

restrictions.conservation_area: Roof enlargements and dormers in a conservation area face much closer control, especially on principal or highway-facing slopes and where the roofscape is sensitive.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually required for roof alterations or works affecting character, and planning permission may also be needed.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can remove the normal roof-alteration fallback route in selected streets or heritage areas, so check the property's designation before relying on permitted development.
